messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated p95/p99 latency for text-generation streaming (SSE) in us-west-2. Error spike and increased connection backlog. Paging on-call: @taylor_ops. Metrics: 30m window, p99 tokens latency +220% ; SSE connection queue > 2k. Logs: streaming-handler timeouts and OOM-ish traces. :rotating_light:

taylor_ops: got the page, looking. Which customers impacted? any high tier SLA hits?

maria_support: partials from support: 8 customers have reported stalled streaming updates in last 15m, 2 on dedicated, rest hosted. No billing hits reported yet.

sam_platform: confirmed alert, tracing shows a hot shard on gpu-pool-usw2-3 causing tail latency. Non-streaming responses still working but with higher token latency. suspect continuous batching + KV eviction thrash.

meera_frontend: we're seeing client retries and some UIs fall back to 'loading' spinner. Could be bad UX if we toggle. Need messaging to customers if we disable streaming.

sam_platform: mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily disable streaming SSE endpoints for public hosted API in us-west-2 2) shift traffic to non-streaming (buffered) mode + enable stricter per-key rate limit for chat/streaming routes 3) enable prefix caching on common prompts 4) monitor p99 and backlog; rollback after stabilization.

meera_frontend: prefer targeted disable for only hosted public streaming, keep Dedicated and Private untouched if possible. Also add a Canary: disable for 90% of traffic, keep 10% streaming to monitor quality.

inc-bot: ACTIONS: created incident-2003456789 in ops. Pager escalation to @taylor_ops and @sam_platform. Runbook: "temporarily_disable_streaming" link: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/streaming-mitigation

sam_platform: I can toggle feature-flag via admin API. Running dry-run to check config:

```
# curl (internal admin)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/feature-flags/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"streaming.public.usw2","enabled":false,"scope":"percentage","value":90}'
```

sam_platform: executing now. Will publish in stages (canary 10% streaming) and watch backlog.

deploy-bot: deploy started: ff-toggle/streaming.public.usw2 -> rollout id ff-req-8812. Rollout eta ~ 30s.

meera_frontend: heads-up for customer-facing: preparing a short banner: "Temporarily disabling live streaming in US-West to improve stability. Responses will be delivered after generation completes. We expect <30m."

sam_platform: toggle completed. Verified admin response: {"status":"rolling_out","rollout_id":"ff-req-8812","enabled":false,"scope":"percentage","value":90}. Canary group (10%) still streaming.

maria_support: posting support note to affected customers now. Mentioning degraded streaming and fallback.

sam_platform: immediate metrics: SSE connection backlog dropped from 2.1k -> 680 in 3m. p99 token latency down ~35% on canary-shard vs pre-change. Errors decreased.

meera_frontend: telemetry from web clients: retry loops reduced, UX spinner clears faster. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: NOTE: increased rate limit applied for streaming routes: new limits for hosted-usw2: 40 requests/min per key (was 60) for chat/streaming; non-streaming endpoints unchanged. Applied via rate-limiter config push id rl-442.

sam_platform: pushing prefix cache for common prompts in us-west-2 (quick patch). Command:

```
POST /internal/cache/prefixs
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY
Body: {"prefixes":["summarize:","translate:"]}
```

meera_frontend: support reporting: initial OOO customers notified, only one dedicated customer requested to remain on streaming — they were grandfathered and kept on Dedicated pool (no change).

maria_support: current count: ~270 hosted API keys impacted in region, 8 support tickets opened, 2 escalations. We're sending status updates.

sam_platform: monitoring: p99 across generation endpoints (hosted-usw2) now trending down. CPU/GPU queue lengths reduced. Still watching for KV thrash.

meera_frontend: ops dashboards look stable. Do we want to extend rate limits or change quota windows?

sam_platform: hold changes for 10m; if stable, we'll keep streaming disabled for up to 45m and then re-enable via canary. If improved, we'll increase streaming percentage slowly (25% -> 50% -> 100%). If regress, revert to full disable and open a deeper RCA.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place: streaming 90% disabled in hosted-usw2, rate limits tightened. No data exfil or security concerns. Impact: degraded UX for affected hosted customers, no data loss.

maria_support: posting status page update: "Investigating streaming instability; temporary switch to buffered responses for impacted region. ETA 30-45m."

sam_platform: 12m after toggle: backlog down to 320, p99 latency down 48%, error rate down 60%. Decision: begin slow re-enable to 25% streaming after additional 8m observation.

deploy-bot: rollout updated: ff-req-8812 -> set value 75 (means 25% disabled)? Confirm command:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/feature-flags/toggle -d '{"flag":"streaming.public.usw2","enabled":true,"scope":"percentage","value":25}'
```

sam_platform: applied. Now 25% streaming. Monitoring...

meera_frontend: customer messaging updated: we will remove banner when we hit ~90% restoration.

inc-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF: @taylor_ops handing to @sam_platform for steady-state monitoring.

maria_support: keeping a watch on tickets; prepared escalation to SOC if errors spike.

sam_platform: after 25% rollout, metrics stable. Plan to restore to 50% in 10m, then 100% if no regress. Will file incident postmortem and include KV cache tuning and autoscaling adjustment as action items.

meera_frontend: note for postmortem: include customer communication timeline and recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance.

sam_platform: final note: temporary mitigation worked as intended — disabling streaming reduced internal queuing and p99. Recommend follow-up: refine batching thresholds, adjust KV cache TTLs, and add a circuit-breaker to auto-fallback streaming when queue depth > 1k.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: streaming restored gradually; monitoring for 2h. Incident closed status will be set after postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:"
